title: Weak poset chains normalize naturally to augmented strict chains
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. For each finite partially ordered set $S$, possibly empty, define $W_n(S;R)$ for $n\geq0$ to be the free $R$-module on all weakly increasing tuples $(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$ in $S$, with no tuples killed. Put $W_{-1}(S;R)=R[\varnothing]$ and $W_n(S;R)=0$ for $n<-1$. Define $d_n[x_0,\ldots,x_n]=\sum_{j=0}^n(-1)^j[x_0,\ldots,\widehat{x_j},\ldots,x_n]$ for $n\geq0$, where the deletion of a vertex is the empty tuple, and put $d_n=0$ for $n<0$. For $n\geq1$ let $D_n(S;R)$ be the span of the tuples with a repeated entry; set $D_n(S;R)=0$ for $n\leq0$. Then $d^2=0$, so $W(S;R)$ is an integer-indexed chain complex [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology], and $d_nD_n(S;R)\subseteq D_{n-1}(S;R)$. Let $C(S;R)$ be the augmented strict-chain complex [def-sfb-augmented-poset-chains]. The map $q_S:W(S;R)\to C(S;R)$ which kills every repeated tuple, sends every strict tuple to its strict-chain generator, and fixes $[\varnothing]$, is a surjective chain map with degreewise kernel $D(S;R)$; it induces an isomorphism of chain complexes $\overline q_S:W(S;R)/D(S;R)\xrightarrow{\sim} C(S;R)$. For every monotone map $u:S\to T$ of finite posets, entrywise image $W(u)_n[x_0,\ldots,x_n]=[u(x_0),\ldots,u(x_n)]$, with $W(u)_{-1}=\mathrm{id}_R$ and zero in lower degrees, is a chain map carrying $D_n(S;R)$ into $D_n(T;R)$. These maps satisfy $W(\mathrm{id}_S)=\mathrm{id}$ and $W(v\circ u)=W(v)\circ W(u)$ for every composable pair of monotone maps. Under $\overline q_S$ and $\overline q_T$, the map induced on the quotient sends a strict generator to its entrywise image when that image is strict and to zero otherwise, and fixes the empty generator.

source.place: Tag 019S, lemma-homotopy-s-N, and preceding equation-homotopy-to-homotopy (lines 4739–4846): prism boundary cancellation. Extracted from the returned item, old proof steps 1–4: double-deletion cancellation, repeated-tuple subcomplex, quotient identification, and entrywise functoriality.

proof.text: Deleting an entry preserves weak increase, so the displayed formula extends linearly to $d_n$. For $n\geq1$, each pair of original positions $a<b$ appears twice in $d_{n-1}d_n$: delete $a$ then position $b-1$, with coefficient $(-1)^{a+b-1}$, or delete $b$ then position $a$, with coefficient $(-1)^{a+b}$. The resulting tuples coincide and the coefficients sum to zero. This includes $n=1$, where both results are the empty tuple. For $n\leq0$ the composite is zero since $d_{-1}=0$ and lower terms vanish. This gives a complex with the convention of [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. The Lean proof packages the signed face sum as A(l,F). The identity A(a::l,F)=F(l)-A(l,t↦F(a::t)) follows by separating deletion of the head. Induction on l, using additivity in F, proves A(l,t↦A(t,F))=0. Apply this with F(t)=[t] in the target weak-chain degree; valid deletions have the required weak order and length. This proves all adjacent-degree composites, and the other composites vanish by the shape condition. This is the same double-deletion cancellation without a two-index reindexing.

source.place: Tag 0194, section-complexes, lines 3605–3648: alternating double-deletion cancellation; the augmentation and integer-index extension are checked explicitly.

proof.text: If $x_a=x_b$ with $a<b$ in a weak tuple, then $x_a\leq x_{a+1}\leq x_b=x_a$, so antisymmetry gives an adjacent equality $x_a=x_{a+1}$. Fix this pair. The two faces deleting position $a$ or $a+1$ are identical with opposite coefficients. Every other deletion retains both equal entries and hence is repeated. Thus $d_nD_n\subseteq D_{n-1}$ for $n\geq2$. When $n=1$, the repeated generator is $[x,x]$ and its boundary is $[x]-[x]=0\in D_0$. For $n\leq0$ the source $D_n$ is zero. In the Lean proof, first establish the degreewise kernel identification without boundary laws: send each strict generator to its identical weak generator. Projection after this section is the identity; after projection followed by the section, a weak generator differs from itself only by a repeated generator. Therefore the projection kernel is exactly D. The adjacent-pair cancellation shows the strict projection of a repeated boundary is zero, so the kernel identification gives preservation of D. There is no dependence on an assumed boundary law in this kernel calculation.

source.place: Tag 0FKI, remark-degenerate-subcomplex, lines 3898–3915, and the adjacent equal-face cancellation immediately preceding it; explicit augmented poset adaptation.

proof.text: By [def-sfb-augmented-poset-chains], every deletion of a strict tuple is again strict (including the empty face of a vertex). Hence $q_{n-1}d_n=d^C_nq_n$ on strict generators. On repeated generators the right side is zero, and the left side is zero by step 2 because $q$ kills $D_{n-1}$. In degree $-1$ both differentials are zero, and lower modules are zero. Thus $q$ is a chain map; it is surjective since each strict basis vector, and the empty generator, is its own tuple image. For the repeated case, the Lean proof first proves a general list identity: whenever F vanishes on repeated lists, A(p++[a,a]++s,F)=0. The two leading equal faces cancel when p is empty, and induction removes the prefix p. Take F to be the strict bracket. This establishes the projection chain-map equation directly, before deducing the repeated-submodule preservation from its kernel.

source.place: Tags 0194 (section-complexes) and 0FKI (remark-degenerate-subcomplex); generator-by-generator comparison with the stated strict-chain definition.

proof.text: In every nonnegative degree the weak basis is the disjoint union of strict tuples and repeated tuples: for unequal entries, weak increase gives strict increase. Any element has a unique finite expansion in this basis. Its $q$-image is zero exactly when every strict coefficient vanishes, since the strict generators form the basis of $C_n$ in [def-sfb-augmented-poset-chains]. Thus $\ker q_n=D_n$. In degree $-1$, $q_{-1}$ is the identity and $D_{-1}=0$; below it both terms vanish. On $W_n/D_n$, define $\overline q_n([w])=q_n(w)$, well defined because $q_n(D_n)=0$. The inverse sends a strict basis vector to the class of the same tuple, and the empty generator to its class. Both composites are identities: repeated classes are zero and strict classes span the quotient. The quotient differential $[w]\mapsto[d_nw]$ is well defined by step 2. The equation in step 3 shows that these inverse degreewise maps commute with the differentials (apply the inverse to that equation), giving the asserted isomorphism of complexes. The Lean construction uses the quotient lift of the explicitly defined projection. Its kernel is zero by the kernel computation and it is surjective by the strict-to-weak section. LinearEquiv.ofBijective supplies its uniquely determined inverse; HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents assembles the degreewise isomorphisms using the projection chain-map equation. Quotient shape, square-zero and map commutation are proved by taking representatives.

source.place: Tag 0FKI, remark-degenerate-subcomplex; agent-written basis proof of the quotient comparison, including degree -1, rather than an application of a general normalization theorem.

proof.text: Monotonicity of $u$ makes $u(x_0),\ldots,u(x_n)$ weakly increasing. Entrywise application commutes with deletion, with the same position and sign, so $d_nW(u)_n=W(u)_{n-1}d_n$ on every weak generator for $n\geq1$. For $n=0$ both sides send a vertex to the empty generator, and negative degrees have zero differentials. This is exactly the chain-map condition in [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Equal source entries have equal images, so repeated generators map into $D_n(T)$. In nonpositive degrees both $D$ terms are zero. Applying identity or composable maps entrywise gives $W(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$ and $W(v\circ u)=W(v)W(u)$ on each basis element; the formulas are also identities on degree $-1$ and on zero modules below it.

source.place: Tag 0194, section-complexes, lines 3640–3648: functoriality; entrywise deletion, augmentation, and repetition preservation verified directly.

proof.text: Since $W(u)(D(S))\subseteq D(T)$, the formula $[w]\mapsto[W(u)w]$ defines the quotient map and commutes with the quotient differential by step 5. Under step 4, a strict source generator is represented by precisely its tuple, whose image is its entrywise $u$-tuple. If that image is strict, its class corresponds to the strict generator of [def-sfb-augmented-poset-chains]; if it has a repetition, its class is zero. These are the only possibilities for a weak tuple. The empty generator is fixed because $W(u)_{-1}=\mathrm{id}_R$. This proves the asserted compatibility.
